tagline: 118 islands across the South Pacific — the Society Islands move on water.
summary: French Polynesia spreads 118 islands and atolls across an expanse of the South Pacific the size of Western Europe. Its tourism heart — the Society Islands of Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Raiatea and Taha'a — is among the world's most coveted luxury-travel destinations, and every journey between them is a water or air leg. Today that movement runs on inter-island ferries and small aircraft. A clean, stabilised foiling tier is the premium layer between the ferry and the floatplane.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief tells the Polynesian story, because it IS the lagoon and the channel between the Society Islands. Tahiti to Moorea is a short, busy crossing; the run from Bora Bora to Raiatea and Taha'a threads some of the most beautiful water on Earth. The ultra-luxury resorts of Bora Bora and the Tuamotus depend on transfers that today mean a shared ferry or a small plane. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns these crossings into smooth, dry, discreet glides matched to the destination's standard.

demand_signals.label: Ultra-luxury resort density
demand_signals.note: Bora Bora and the Society Islands host some of the world's most prestigious overwater-villa resorts, whose guests expect premium, discreet transfers.

demand_signals.label: Inter-island travel necessity
demand_signals.note: Every multi-island itinerary — the overwhelming majority of visits — requires water or air legs between islands.

demand_signals.label: Island-community links
demand_signals.note: The Society and Tuamotu island communities rely on inter-island boats for people and goods — core infrastructure across vast distances.

demand_signals.label: Experience-led travel
demand_signals.note: Polynesia's visitors travel for the water itself; a clean, quiet, beautiful crossing is part of the product, not just transport.

use_cases.body: Tahiti (Papeete) to Moorea: the busy ~12-nautical-mile gateway crossing, today a frequent ferry — ideal for a smooth, dry, premium foiling shuttle.
Bora Bora to Raiatea: a ~24-nautical-mile Society Islands hop linking the marquee lagoon to its neighbours, comfortably inside Pioneer II range.
Bora Bora to Taha'a: a ~21-nautical-mile crossing to the vanilla island and its luxury resorts — a discreet premium transfer over spectacular water.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core Society Islands crossings — Tahiti–Moorea (~12 nm), Bora Bora–Raiatea (~24 nm), Bora Bora–Taha'a (~21 nm) — sit comfortably inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long reaches toward the Tuamotu atolls (Rangiroa, Tikehau, Fakarava) are Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening atoll trunks no day-boat can serve.

signature_routes.label: Bora Bora ↔ Raiatea — the Society Islands hop
Bora Bora ↔ Taha'a — the vanilla-island link

transit_planning: For a luxury-resort operator or a tourism authority: a clean, quiet, low-emission water tier that matches the standard of Polynesia's overwater resorts and turns the inter-island transfer into part of the experience. Start with the proven Society Islands crossings on Pioneer II, then reach the Tuamotu atolls on Quanta-LR as range comes online.
competitive_landscape: Inter-island travel today splits between inter-island ferries (affordable but utilitarian) and small aircraft / floatplanes (fast but expensive and weather-limited). Navier's foiling tier is the missing premium-but-practical middle: smoother and drier than a ferry, far more attainable and lower-impact than air, and matched to a destination where the water is the point.
regulatory_note: French Polynesia is an overseas collectivity of France with its own competencies; maritime transport operates under French and territorial maritime-safety frameworks, requiring vessel certification and route authorisation. The territorial government's maritime affairs directorate is the natural first touchpoint.
seasonality: The dry season (May–Oct) brings the calmest lagoons and channels and peak demand; the wetter, warmer months (Nov–Apr) carry higher humidity and occasional tropical systems. Sheltered lagoon and inter-island routes remain navigable year-round.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to Polynesia's luxury resorts.
